label: After the mapper fix the OpenCode plugin head and the Claude hook head are byte-identical across nine prompt classes (typed 286 B, plain 286 B, ambiguous 305 B, doctor 298 B, no-match 244 B, /deep:research plain 294 B, /deep:review plain 292 B, /deep:ai-council plain 296 B, doctor-deep-loop plain 293 B); command, policy word and owner all match.

The plugin emits a second system block the hook never emits: 'Compiled routing (served=compiled): hub=sk-doc outcome=route targets=none', 73 bytes, on the first prompt and on every repeat, so OpenCode receives 73 more bytes per prompt than Claude for the same routing decision and the line carries no target information in this measurement.

Repeat reduction has the same shape in both paths (head kept, directive block dropped: 286 B to 68 B in the plugin) but a different reset trigger: the plugin resets on startup, resume, compact, generation or epoch change, while the Claude hook also resets when the transcript file shrinks.

The two paths read pass thresholds from different places: the hook recomputes passes_threshold from data.effectiveThresholds echoed by the CLI, while the plugin ignores effectiveThresholds and hardcodes uncertainty 0.35; with the workspace defaults the echoed thresholds were 0.8/0.35 on every probe prompt, so the outputs agreed and only a workspace override would diverge.

The request shapes differ in three fields: the hook sends includeCompiledRoute and compiledRouteTopOnly, the plugin sends neither and adds surfaceHint; the measured effect on nine prompts is none because the handler attaches the command before the compiled route is consulted, so the difference is latent rather than active.

Delivery channel and position differ even when the bytes do not: the hook returns hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext on the user-prompt event while the plugin pushes onto output.system in experimental.chat.system.transform, and the OpenCode copy exists only in memory, which is why the 24 OpenCode rows of the committed arm still read briefDelivered unknown.

The fail-open text is a second implementation held equal by a parity test, not a shared one: the plugin imports renderPluginFallbackDirective from a plugin-local module while the hook uses renderAdvisorFallbackDirective from the shared renderer; the measured no-match fallback is 244 bytes on both.

Three smaller asymmetries are inert today: the plugin drops kind and heldBelow which the renderer copies but never reads for a label, the plugin clamps the brief at 2048 characters where the hook relies on the 480-character token cap, and the plugin caches the brief for five minutes per session and prompt so a route change inside the TTL is invisible to OpenCode and visible to Claude.

The child-session rewrite is shared and correctly applied by both paths: with AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 both rendered /create:readme as parent-named only and without the marker both rendered start, so the two failing brief test files the phase-013 summary records are an environment effect rather than a caller difference.
